title: Internal Hom through the coefficient dual
statement:
Let $p,\ell$ be distinct primes, let $a,n\geq1$ be integers, put $q=p^a$, let $k_0=\mathbf F_q$ and $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$, and let $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ be a finite extension with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi_E$. Put $A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$ and choose $\Lambda\in\{A_{E,n},\mathcal O_E,E,\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell\}$. Fix a six-functor datum [def-sf-datum] on separated finite-type $k$-schemes, with the coefficient categories, tensor and internal Hom of [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom], and let $X$ be a scheme in this datum. Write $\Lambda_X$ for its coefficient unit (the constant finite coefficient sheaf at finite level and the completed coefficient sheaf at integral level, with rational and common-stage images at the field levels). Let $K\in D^b_{ctf}(X,\Lambda)$ be quasi-isomorphic, locally on the coefficient site of $X$, to a bounded complex of finite projective $\Lambda_X$-modules: the local terms are direct summands of finite sums of the coefficient unit, with the localized and common-stage interpretations of [def-weil-site-perfect-complex]. Put $K^\vee=R\mathcal Hom_X(K,\Lambda_X)$. Then for every $M\in D^b_{ctf}(X,\Lambda)$ the canonical evaluation comparison
$$
K^\vee\otimes^L_{\Lambda_X}M\longrightarrow R\mathcal Hom_X(K,M)
$$
is an isomorphism.

proof.text: At finite and integral coefficients, apply the proved ringed-site perfect-duality theorem to the specified ambient model. The recorded site-perfect predicates are exactly its hypotheses. Reflect its all-target evaluation isomorphism to the finite-Tor full subcategory through the fully faithful normalized closed embedding.

For any finite coefficient field and its normalized coefficient closed models, local rational evaluation is invertible on a covering. Rational cover detection gives global invertibility in the constructible category; its full-subcategory inclusion reflects this. Use this argument both for E and for every coefficient subfield of Qbar.
Apply common-stage descent to the rational evaluation isomorphisms just obtained at all finite coefficient fields. Combine the four conclusions.

proof_origin.place: Finite-projective evaluation and bounded-complex argument, with the ringed-site calculation reused and the rational local calculation, global detection and common-stage descent separated.

split_report.summary: Repaired the returned split by extracting the hidden non-elementary arguments of former steps 8 and 9 into four statement-only lemma nodes: slice compatibility of completed and rational operations, triangulated closure of the rational evaluation class, finite-cover power-torsion detection, and bounded-cone torsion via truncations. Replaced the two overlong steps by six shorter steps preserving the original finite-level, integral, rational, and common-stage route. Maintainer reader (2026-10-17): steps 8-12 and three of the new statements recast in the ambient scalar localizations of the derived categories on slices, so that the local rational argument needs no constructibility of slice internal Homs; stale tool uses of the former step 9 removed.
split_report.blueprint: Finite-level local calculation in steps 1–6, integral reduction in step 7, rational slice compatibility and bounded-complex induction in steps 8–10, finite-cover detection and bounded-cone torsion in steps 11–13, and common-field passage in step 14. The route and proposition statement are unchanged.

tool_uses.why: Ordinary evaluation for a sheaf retract of a finite free module, valid for arbitrary target module sheaves; supplies the termwise calculation in the unit, not a replacement route.
Finite-filtration theorem for Hom complexes with exact termwise Hom; justifies the unit's passage from a bounded local model to derived Hom.
Bounded-above flat complexes are K-flat on any ringed site; justifies the local dual tensor representative.
Canonical computation of derived tensor using K-flat flat-term representatives.
Exactness of slice restriction, used for local calculation and local cohomology-sheaf detection.

Monoidality of derived pullback for ringed topoi, applied to slice restriction.
Identifies finite reductions and scalar extensions of the actual dual/evaluation map, retaining the completed tensor at integral coefficients.
Ensures the cone of the integral comparison is derived complete, so reduction detects its vanishing.
Exactness of the derived reduction functor, used on the integral comparison cone.
Existence of flat-term K-flat resolutions for arbitrary complexes on a ringed site.
Exact termwise countable products in the pro-etale module category justify that the Roos construction commutes with finite mapping cones.
Exact scalar extension preserves the rational finite-filtration argument and the common coefficient field.
Bounds the cohomology of a derived-complete representative from its uniformly bounded reductions.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q94-7436887f3 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the item, all four new nodes, the unit and chapter, the master and main-20261015 blueprint text, Stacks 08JJ and every cited statement in full. Steps 1-7, 13 and 14 are correct: I recomputed the signs in steps 4-5 (both components give (-1)^{ij}), and the bound of step 13, H^d(C)=0 outside [u,v+1], follows from the integral-category amplitude, exact countable products and the long exact sequence. The item statement is unchanged and not weakened. Fault 1 (E1/C4): step 10 applied the closure clauses of lem-sf-rational-thick-evaluation, which hold only 'whenever the objects lie in their stated domains', to sigma_{>=r}P and P^r[-r] on slices. The rational RHom (def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom) is defined only for pairs whose integral internal Hom is constructible, and nothing shows this on non-quasi-compact weakly etale slices. A rational retract of a constructible object need not be integrally constructible (Y+T with T a varpi^c-torsion object). For the same reason, local-global-power-torsion assumed slice constructibility and slice-completed-evaluation asserted it with no precise meaning. Repair: steps 8-12 and these three new statements now work in the ambient scalar localizations D(slice, O^)[1/varpi], where the completed tensor and RHom are always defined and the localization is triangulated. D^b_c(X,E) embeds fully there, so global invertibility is unchanged. The thick lemma now takes M derived complete, which the unit clause and the adjunct need. Local-global takes any C, with zero image equivalent to varpi^{N_j} id = 0. The slice lemma now asserts derived completeness of the restrictions, which is true because j^* is exact and sectionwise. Step 12 now justifies the finite covering by separatedness of X, and step 11 states the domain presupposition. Fault 2 (brief section 3): all four new nodes lacked merged_into and lean_audit; both are added. Three stale tool uses from the former step 9 are removed. All four new statements are true and were tested on small cases: N=0, u=v, C=0, t=0/X empty, a point. They are statement-only, strictly smaller than the item and duplicate nothing: grep of power-torsion, thick and Roos/slice nodes; lem-sf-generating-class-determination supplies only the formal closure. I accept the 14 remaining tool uses. No SGA source is used. Corrected files are in fixes/dag/nodes/sec-six-functors/ (the item and the four new nodes).; 5 file(s) fixed by the reviewer
